title: Islanded-error Isolation and Low-effort Fix Prioritization
content:
Context:
This doc records an exploratory deep-dive into small, concentrated clusters of onboarding/regression failures we observed across the December seed eval. We call these clusters "islands": semantically-tight prompt neighborhoods that produce high severity but low-volume failures (often missed during broad aggregate metrics). Goal: isolate islands, hypothesize minimal root causes, and propose low-effort fixes we can roll out quickly with measurable guardrails.

Summary findings (top level):
- Islands exist across three surface areas: (1) short-instruction ambiguity (1–3 token diff flips), (2) numeric/date formatting edgecases, (3) persona/context bleed when system prompt is weak.
- Simple heuristics recover 40–80% of island failure incidents with negligible latency impact; higher-reliability fixes need small prompt-set rewriters or targeted LoRA fine-tunes (costly).
- Recommended initial program: (A) island detector + soft-routing to fallback policy, (B) prioritized list of 6 low-effort fixes with expected ROI and test plan, (C) continuous micro-eval to avoid regressions.

How islands were identified (method):
1) Collect failure set: seed onboarding eval + first 72h production anomalies filtered by regression signal scores > 0.2 and human severity >= 2.
2) Represent inputs with hybrid features: sentence-BERT embedding (for semantics), shingled token n-grams (character bigrams), and a compact metadata vector encoded as categorical tokens (lang, length-bin, intent-type).
3) Dimensionality reduction: UMAP (n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1) on concatenated feature vector; cluster with HDBSCAN (min_cluster_size=8).
4) Post-filter: clusters with failure rate > 65% and at least 12 examples were flagged as islands.
5) Validation: manual read of 30 random samples per island and attention/kv-cache inspection on representative failure traces.

Sample islands (representative):
- Island A: "Imperative-short"
  - Pattern: user prompts that are 3–6 tokens, start with an imperative but omit the object (e.g., "Summarize quickly:", "Give steps:"). Model responds with meta-text or asks clarifying question instead of the requested short summary.
  - Hypothesis: System prompt instructs for clarifying questions for underspecified requests; gateway detector is too sensitive for short-form tasks.
  - Quick fixes proposed: (1) detect short-imperative pattern and apply a compressed prefix that forces concise completion (example prefix: "Return a one-line summary: "), (2) increase top-p floor for these inputs to discourage question-asking.
  - Expected ROI: 70% fix rate on island samples; negligible infra impact.

- Island B: "Numeric-format drift"
  - Pattern: short finance-related prompts where user provides currency/date in non-standard forms (e.g., "reconcile 10k vs 10,000") causing misinterpretation and hallucinated conversions.
  - Hypothesis: Tokenization boundary and custom numeracy handling in the model leads to misalignment with canonical representation; tokenizer splits cause attention distortions.
  - Quick fixes proposed: (1) a light preprocessor normalizer (regex-based) to canonicalize numbers/dates before send, (2) add deterministic-k decoding for numeric tokens (bias logits for canonical format).
  - Expected ROI: ~60% immediate reduction in severity; + small latency for preprocessing.

- Island C: "System prompt leakage for persona-heavy tasks"
  - Pattern: customer prompts referencing company-name or role and expecting role-play; model returns disallowed content or vendor-specific suggestions due to subtle system prompt mismatch.
  - Hypothesis: system instruction contains a long list of banned behaviors; for certain prompt shapes the decode policy flips and model over-censors or generates policy evasive language.
  - Quick fixes proposed: (1) short-term: explicit role prefix insertion ("You are a friendly product assistant. Answer concisely."), (2) mid-term: create per-route policy-sensitivity weights and softfallback to a less-restrictive variant when confidence is low.
  - Expected ROI: 50–80% depending on route composition.

Prioritization framework for fixes (how we chose the low-effort list):
- Low-effort criteria: changeable in the serving layer without retraining, reversible, testable via canary.
- Priority score = (impact_estimate * severity_weight) / implementation_cost_estimate.
- Implementation cost buckets: trivial (regex/prefix) = 1, small infra change (decode biasing, routing) = 3, model change (LoRA/tune) = 8.

Proposed quick-fix catalog (ranked):
1) Short-imperative prefix insertion (island A) — trivial. Add a small rule in request preprocessing to detect imperative templates and prepend a concise-output instruction. Triage: create canary with 10% traffic for 48h.
2) Numeric/date canonicalizer (island B) — trivial. Regex-based normalizer with opt-out header in request to preserve original text.
3) Route-level decode-bias for numerics (island B) — small infra change. Modify logits for tokens matching numeric canonical forms when metadata indicates numeric intent.
4) Confidence-based soft-routing (island C) — small infra change. Route low-confidence outputs to fallback model variant that has reduced safety sensitivity for developer routes.
5) Prompt set augmentation for failing archetypes — small infra change. Insert 10–30 synthetic prompts into onboarding eval and track regression delta post-fix.
6) Targeted LoRA on 5k island examples — model change, high cost. Reserve only if quick fixes fail.

Test & rollout plan (detailed):
- Per-fix quick A/B: create paired prompt set subsets (island-only and random baseline) and measure pass-rate delta, latency, token-cost delta.
- Canary window: 48–72 hours with 5–15% traffic depending on perceived risk; enable automatic rollback if severity increases by >10% or latency >15% over baseline.
- Evaluation metrics: pass_rate (binary human label), avg_response_latency, token_count_per_request, false_block_rate (for policy-sensitive fixes).
- Post-rollout: add augmented examples from live failures to the seed eval and re-run clustering monthly to detect island drift.

Monitoring & guardrails:
- Implement an island-alert hook: when any HDBSCAN cluster surpasses an island threshold (failure_rate>50% & size>=10), create automated ticket with top-10 exemplar prompts attached.
- Add a lightweight model-introspection log: attention entropy for the top-3 tokens and prefix-match flag for inputs subject to a heuristic fix. Store for 7 days by default, 30 days for flagged islands.

Open questions & unknowns (need experiments):
- How often do islands migrate across clusters after a quick fix? (risk: splitting creates many micro-islands)
- Numeric canonicalizer failure modes: does normalization remove fidelity for legal/financial contexts? Need opt-out semantics.
- Soft-routing safety: measure leakage risk if fallback is less-restrictive — run adversarial prompts in canary.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- [Avery Chen] implement short-imperative detector + prefix insertion prototype (ETA: 1 week) — GH PR and canary config.
- [Maya Patel] numeric canonicalizer regex set + unit tests (ETA: 10 days) — include opt-out header.
- [Jordan Brooks] route-level decode-bias spike experiment and metrics pipeline (ETA: 2 weeks) — coordinate with infra.
- [Ravi Gupta] monitoring hook and island-alert automation (ETA: 3 weeks) — connect to JIRA pipeline.

Appendix: example detection regexes and heuristic pseudocode (short):
- Imperative detection: ^( (Summariz|Summarize|Give|List|Explain|Provide|Define) ).length <= 12 tokens => short-imperative = true
- Numeric canonicalizer examples: replace ([0-9]{1,3})(,([0-9]{3}))+ => collapse to digits-only; standardize k/K suffixes to explicit thousands; parse currencies with localized rule table.

Closing notes:
This doc is intentionally pragmatic — the goal is to deploy a set of reversible, minimal-risk changes that capture quick wins against concentrated failure islands while preserving our longer-term evaluation and tuning runway. If quick fixes do not hit the expected ROI within 2 canary cycles, we escalate to model-level interventions.

References and artifacts: see linked_artifacts above for dashboards, PR drafts and the Jira epic.
